label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. For every $N\ge2$ and every $s\ge1$, there exists a nonempty dense Zariski-open subset $U$ of the parameter space of $s$ distinct points in $\mathbb P^N_\Bbbk$ such that for every $X\in U$, with defining ideal $I_X$, one has
$$
I_X^{(Nr)}\subseteq \mathfrak m^{r(N-1)}I_X^r
$$
for every integer $r\ge1$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: A property of $s$-point configurations holds for \emph{general points} if it holds on a nonempty dense Zariski-open subset of $\mathcal P_{N,s}$. It holds for \emph{very general points} if it holds on a countable intersection of nonempty dense Zariski-open subsets. The \emph{generic points} are the universal ordered configuration over the function field of $\mathcal P_{N,s}$.
head: environment

label: lem:regcriterion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:regcriterion}
Let $I\subset R$ be a homogeneous ideal with zero-dimensional support. If $q,r,k$ are nonnegative integers and
$$
\alpha(I^{(q)})>r\,\operatorname{reg}(I)+k,
$$
then
$$
I^{(q)}\subseteq \mathfrak m^kI^r.
$$
head: environment
name: degree-to-containment criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
For completeness, we recall the argument. Since
$$
\alpha(I^{(q)})\le q\alpha(I)\le q\operatorname{reg}(I),
$$
the assumed inequality forces $q\ge r$, hence $I^{(q)}\subseteq I^{(r)}=\operatorname{sat}(I^r)$. For ideals with zero-dimensional support one has
$$
\operatorname{satdeg}(I^r)\le\operatorname{reg}(I^r)\le r\operatorname{reg}(I).
$$
Thus $I^{(r)}$ and $I^r$ agree in degrees above $r\operatorname{reg}(I)$. Moreover $I^r$ is generated in degrees at most $r\operatorname{reg}(I)$. Consequently every element of $I^{(q)}$ occurs only in degrees greater than $r\operatorname{reg}(I)+k$ and, in those degrees, lies in $\mathfrak m^k I^r$.
head: environment

label: lem:openalpha
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:openalpha}
Fix an integer $m\ge1$. There is a nonempty dense Zariski-open subset $U_m\subset\mathcal P_{N,s}$ such that, for every $X\in U_m$,
$$
\alpha(I_X^{(m)})=\alpha(H^{(m)}).
$$
There is also a nonempty dense open subset $U_{\rm reg}$ on which
$$
\operatorname{reg}(I_X)=\operatorname{reg}(H).
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each degree $d$, the vector space $(I_X^{(m)})_d$ is the kernel of the jet-evaluation map that sends a degree-$d$ form to its derivatives of order $<m$ at the $s$ points. After choosing affine charts locally on $\mathcal P_{N,s}$, this is a matrix whose entries are regular functions in the point coordinates. Its rank is maximal at the generic point and therefore constant on a nonempty open subset. Taking the finite intersection of these open sets for all degrees up to $\alpha(H^{(m)})$ gives the first assertion.

The second assertion follows in the same way from the generic Hilbert function, or from the usual semicontinuity of cohomology in the universal family of reduced points. Only finitely many degrees up to the generic regularity are involved.
head: environment

label: rem:noinfinite
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:noinfinite}
The finiteness in Lemma~\ref{lem:openalpha} is crucial. There is in general no reason that one can choose one open set on which $\alpha(I_X^{(m)})$ agrees with the generic value simultaneously for every $m$. Doing so by intersecting the individual open sets produces a very general condition. Our argument below deliberately chooses one symbolic level before specializing.
head: environment

label: prop:upgrade
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: finite-open upgrade

label: eq:finitegap
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $R_0=\operatorname{reg}(H)$. Since $c_m(H)\to\widehat\alpha(H)$ and the inequality in \eqref{eq:genericgap} is strict, there is an integer $m_0\ge1$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finitegap}
Nc_{m_0}(H)>R_0+N-1.
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:openalpha}, after replacing $\mathcal P_{N,s}$ by a nonempty dense open subset $U$, we may assume simultaneously that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:openconditions}
\alpha(I_X^{(m_0)})=\alpha(H^{(m_0)})
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{reg}(I_X)=R_0.
\end{equation}
for every $X\in U$. In particular,
$$
c_{m_0}(I_X)=c_{m_0}(H).
$$

Fix $X\in U$ and write $I=I_X$. The full Demailly inequality of H\`a--Sivakumar gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:demaillyfiber}
\widehat\alpha(I)\ge c_{m_0}(I)=c_{m_0}(H).
\end{equation}
Since $\widehat\alpha(I)=\inf_q\alpha(I^{(q)})/q$, for every $r\ge1$ we have
$$
\alpha(I^{(Nr)})\ge Nr\widehat\alpha(I)
\ge Nr c_{m_0}(H).
$$
Using \eqref{eq:finitegap} and \eqref{eq:openconditions}, this yields
$$
\alpha(I^{(Nr)})
>r(R_0+N-1)
=r\operatorname{reg}(I)+r(N-1).
$$
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:regcriterion} with $q=Nr$ and $k=r(N-1)$ gives
$$
I^{(Nr)}\subseteq \mathfrak m^{r(N-1)}I^r.
$$
The open set $U$ was chosen before $r$ and is independent of it, so the containment holds there for all $r\ge1$ simultaneously.
head: environment

label: rem:roleDemailly
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:roleDemailly}
For the generic ideal $H$ itself, the strict inequality \eqref{eq:genericgap} already gives
$$
\alpha(H^{(Nr)})\ge Nr\widehat\alpha(H)>r\bigl(\operatorname{reg}(H)+N-1\bigr),
$$
and hence the desired containment for every $r$. Thus the new role of full Demailly is not to prove the all-$r$ statement on the generic fibre. Its role is to make the passage from the generic fibre to \emph{general} fibres finite: one fixed value $\alpha(H^{(m_0)})$ is enough to control every symbolic exponent after specialization.
head: environment

label: thm:newrange
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:newrange}
Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field. Suppose
$$
N\ge4\qquad\text{and}\qquad s\ge N+4.
$$
Then a general set $X$ of $s$ points in $\mathbb P^N_\Bbbk$ satisfies
$$
I_X^{(Nr)}\subseteq \mathfrak m^{r(N-1)}I_X^r
$$
for every $r\ge1$, simultaneously on one dense Zariski-open set of configurations.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $H$ be the ideal of $s$ generic points. Bisui--Nguy\~en prove
$$
\widehat\alpha(H)>\frac{\operatorname{reg}(H)+N-1}{N}
$$
for $N\ge4$ and $s\ge N+4$ \cite[Theorem~4.10]{BN24}. This is exactly the hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:upgrade}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $N=2$, the assertion is the theorem of Harbourne--Huneke for general planar points \cite[Proposition~3.10]{HH13}. If $N=3$, it is due to Dumnicki \cite{Dum12}.

Assume $N\ge4$. For $s\le N+1$, the containment for points in general position was proved by Dumnicki \cite{Dum12}. For $s=N+2$ and $s=N+3$, it follows from Nagel--Trok \cite[Proposition~5.4]{NT19}; their hypotheses are satisfied by a general configuration. Finally, for $s\ge N+4$, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:newrange}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Nagel--Trok actually prove their small-cardinality result for a broader class of linearly general configurations and determine the relevant symbolic initial degrees explicitly \cite[Sections~3--5]{NT19}. Thus there is no hidden specialization issue in the cases $s=N+2,N+3$.
head: environment
